title: ISA (UK and Ireland) 402 (Updated June 2013), Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organization
issuer: Financial Reporting Council (UK), based on IAASB ISA 402
jurisdiction: UK/Ireland (converged with ISA; AU-C 402 is the US clarified counterpart)
summary: User auditor may obtain understanding via a type 1/2 report, by contacting or visiting the service organization and performing procedures, or by using another auditor (para 12). Where controls reliance is planned, evidence of operating effectiveness comes from a type 2 report, own tests, or another auditor's tests (16); evaluate period covered, time elapsed and relevant CUECs (17).

title: AU-C section 402, Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organization (AICPA clarified SAS)
jurisdiction: US (audits of nonprofits and other non-issuers)
pinpoint: Not retrieved: AICPA download is account-gated; DART copy subscription-gated. Paragraph structure stated from memory to parallel ISA 402 paras 12-17.
summary: Governs a nonprofit sponsor's external auditor when the sponsor uses a service organization (e.g. Unbound keeping the DAF ledger). Text not fetched; relied on the converged ISA 402 text (EV-G-001). Treat pinpoints as unverified.

title: PCAOB AS 2601, Consideration of an Entity's Use of a Service Organization
pinpoint: Fetch returned HTTP 403; content known only from search-result summary (user auditor may contact or visit service organization when a service auditor report is unavailable).
summary: Issuer-audit analogue; not applicable to nonprofit sponsors' audits but confirms the same alternatives (contact/visit service organization, request procedures). Not fetched.

title: Appendix A: Comparison of SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC for Cybersecurity Examinations and Related Reports (written statement to ERISA Advisory Council, 2022)
issuer: US Department of Labor EBSA (hosting witness statement reproducing AICPA comparison)
source_type: professional publication reproducing AICPA comparison table
pinpoint: pp.1-3; footnote 1 (inclusive vs carve-out); row 'criteria' (AT-C 320 .15-.17; DC 200; TSP 100 2017 TSC with revised points of focus 2022); row 'purpose'
summary: SOC 1 criteria are in AT-C 320 .15-.17 and the report serves service-org management, user entities and user auditors for ICFR; a type 2 may provide evidence of operating effectiveness. SOC 2 uses DC 200 and TSP 100 (2017 TSC, revised PoF 2022). In SOC 2, management may use inclusive or carve-out method for subservice organizations.

title: The 3 faces of SOC (Journal of Accountancy newsletter, 13 June 2016, archived)
summary: SOC 1 reports on controls relevant to user entities' ICFR, use restricted to service-org management, user entities and user auditors; type 1 as of a date (design), type 2 over a period (operating effectiveness). SOC 2 covers security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality or privacy. Archived; details may be dated.

title: 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (With Revised Points of Focus - 2022)
pinpoint: landing page description; the criteria PDF itself is account-gated
summary: Control criteria established by ASEC for attestation or consulting engagements on controls over a system; five categories. Page landing only; PDF not retrieved.

title: To the Point No. 2022-13: AICPA revises guidance on applying its Trust Services Criteria and SOC 2 Description Criteria (2 Nov 2022)
pinpoint: p.1 'What you need to know'; p.4 SOC 2 guide revisions and endnotes
summary: The AICPA did not change the TSC or SOC 2 Description Criteria in 2022; it updated points of focus and implementation guidance, and revised the SOC 2 guide (TSP 100; DC 200).

title: What Are Bridge (aka Gap) Letters & How Do They Relate to SOC Reports? (M. Kovash, Linford & Co., 2022, updated 2026-06-05)
pinpoint: sections on definition, signer, duration, contents
summary: Bridge letter is signed by service-organization management, not the service auditor, and gives no attestation for the gap; the AICPA does not cover bridge-letter requirements; most cover no more than three months; SOC reports typically cover 6-12 months and recur at least annually.

title: How bridge letters help mind the gap between audit periods (17 Sep 2025)
jurisdiction: UK (practice applies to US SOC reports)
summary: Bridge letters are management-signed, not audit deliverables, with no independent testing; there is no formal guidance, but a statutory auditor generally would not accept one covering more than three months.

title: Considering IT risk during audit risk assessment procedures (D. Arman, AICPA, JofA 1 Nov 2023)
source_type: professional publication by AICPA staff on SAS 145 (AU-C 315)
effective_date: SAS 145 effective for periods ending on or after 2023-12-15 (effective date from memory; article says 'December 2023')
pinpoint: sections on GITCs and system-generated reports
summary: SAS 145 requires auditors to identify IT applications, risks arising from IT and the general IT controls addressing them; ineffective GITCs may preclude reliance on automated controls; reliance on system-generated reports may require testing completeness and accuracy.

title: 8 things to know about the audit evidence standard (B. Dohrer, AICPA Insights, 1 Oct 2023) - SAS No. 142 / AU-C 500
source_type: professional publication by standard setter staff
effective_date: SAS 142 effective for periods ending on or after 2022-12-15
summary: SAS 142 requires considering reliability of information used as audit evidence regardless of source: accuracy, completeness, authenticity and susceptibility to management bias; recognises automated tools and full-population analytics.

title: AU-C 330 (and ISA 330) application material on testing automated controls and reliance on general IT controls
pinpoint: Not retrieved (gated). From memory: application material states that, given the inherent consistency of IT processing, evidence of an automated control's implementation plus effective general IT controls (especially change controls) may provide substantial evidence of operating effectiveness. Paragraph number unverified.
summary: Supports single-instance testing of automated controls when ITGCs are effective. Not fetched; pinpoint unverified.

title: Develop an effective SAP automated controls benchmarking strategy (Protiviti, 16 Nov 2022) citing PCAOB AS 2201 App. B, B28-B33
pinpoint: benchmarking section; AS 2201 B28-B33 reference; re-baselining
summary: Benchmarking (AS 2201 App. B B28-B33): auditor may conclude an automated control remains effective without retesting if ITGCs are effective and the baselined configuration has not changed; re-baselining about every three years is practice, not rule. AS 2201 itself not fetched (PCAOB 403).

title: Internal Control - Integrated Framework: Executive Summary (May 2013)
pinpoint: p.2 (smaller entities); p.4 Control Activities (segregation of duties); p.7 principles 10-12
summary: Framework applies to not-for-profits; smaller entities may be less formal yet effective. Segregation of duties is typically built into control activities; where not practical, management selects and develops alternative control activities. Principle 10 control activities; 11 general controls over technology; 12 policies and procedures.

title: Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government (Green Book), 2025 revision, GAO-25-107721
source_type: internal control standard (binding on federal entities; persuasive elsewhere)
summary: Automated controls tend to be more reliable (10.05). Incompatible duties segregated; where not practical, design alternative controls (10.21, 10.23); separate authority, custody and accounting (10.22). IT segregation: no one individual controls all critical stages, e.g. separate designing, testing and implementing systems (11.16).

title: 8 Del. C. §141 (board of directors; committees) and §142 (officers)
summary: Business and affairs managed by or under the direction of the board except as otherwise provided; committees may exercise board powers as resolution/bylaws provide, except stockholder-approval matters and bylaw changes; §141 applies to nonstock corporations; officers with titles and duties stated in bylaws or board resolution; one person may hold any number of offices.

title: California Corporations Code §5210 (Nonprofit Public Benefit Corporation Law)
issuer: State of California (via california.public.law reproduction, verified 2026-11-16)
summary: Corporate powers exercised by or under the direction of the board; the board may delegate management of activities to any person, management company or committee, provided activities and affairs are managed and powers exercised under the ultimate direction of the board. Official leginfo site returned 403.

title: California Corporations Code §5212 (committees)
summary: Board committees of two or more directors may have board authority except eight listed matters (member-approval actions, vacancies, director compensation, bylaws, non-amendable resolutions, committee appointments, contested-election spending, self-dealing approval); non-director members only on committees without board authority; audit committee where Gov. Code 12586(a) applies.

title: California Corporations Code §5213 (officers)
summary: Required: chair or president, secretary, treasurer or CFO; other officers as bylaws or board provide; one person may hold several offices but secretary/treasurer/CFO cannot be president or chair; officers chosen by and serve at pleasure of the board, subject to contract rights. No requirement that officers be employees.

title: New York Not-for-Profit Corporation Law §701 (board of directors)
summary: Except as otherwise provided in the certificate, a corporation shall be managed by its board; persons other than the board to whom the certificate assigns management bear directors' duties and liabilities.

title: New York Not-for-Profit Corporation Law §712 (executive committee and other committees)
summary: Board committees consist of three or more directors and may not act on listed matters (vacancies, director compensation, bylaws, merger/dissolution, etc.); other committees are committees of the corporation and cannot bind the board.

title: New York Not-for-Profit Corporation Law §713 (officers)
summary: Board may elect or appoint chair/president, vice-presidents, secretary, treasurer and other officers as it determines or bylaws provide; any two offices may be combined except president and secretary; no requirement that officers be directors or employees; employee may chair the board only by two-thirds vote with written reasons.

title: Vermont Nonprofit Corporations Act, 11B V.S.A. chapter 8 (§§8.01, 8.25, 8.40, 8.41) - Model Nonprofit Corporation Act numbering
summary: Powers exercised by or under the authority of the board and affairs managed under its direction; committees may exercise board authority except distributions, fundamental transactions, director elections/vacancies, articles/bylaws; officers appointed by board with duties set by bylaws or board resolution, and the board may authorize an officer to prescribe other officers' duties.

title: Model Nonprofit Corporation Act, Third Edition (2008), §§8.01, 8.25, 8.40, 8.41
issuer: American Bar Association, Business Law Section
pinpoint: Text of §§8.01, 8.25, 8.40-8.41 not retrieved; only bibliographic confirmation that the 3rd edition was adopted Aug 2008.
summary: Model act on which many state nonprofit statutes are based. Section text not fetched; Vermont's statute (EV-G-023) used as the verified example of Model Act numbering. Exact 3rd-edition wording unverified.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4966 (taxes on taxable distributions)
summary: 5% tax on any fund manager agreeing to a distribution knowing it is taxable; joint and several; capped at $10,000 per distribution. Fund manager = officer, director or trustee (or individual with similar powers) and, for any act, employees having authority or responsibility for that act.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4958 (excess benefit transactions)
summary: Organization manager = officer, director or trustee or individual with similar powers; 10% tax on knowing manager participation unless not willful and due to reasonable cause.

title: Treas. Reg. §53.4958-1(d)(2) (organization manager; officer definition)
summary: Officer = person so designated in constitutive documents, or who regularly exercises general authority to make administrative or policy decisions; a contractor acting solely as attorney, accountant or investment manager/advisor is not an officer; someone with authority only to recommend is not an officer.

title: Taxes on Taxable Distributions From Donor Advised Funds Under Section 4966 (NPRM, REG-142338-07), 88 FR 77922 (14 Nov 2023)
pinpoint: Not fetched; existence and docket confirmed via search results; contains proposed fund-manager rules not relied on here.

title: Proposed Rule: Taxes on Taxable Distributions from Donor Advised Funds under Section 4966 (status page, updated 8 May 2026)
summary: States Treasury and IRS have not yet finalized the 2023 proposed §4966 regulations (as of 8 May 2026). No final rule found in searches through 2026-11-24.

title: 26 U.S.C. §170(f)(18) and §170(f)(8)
summary: DAF contribution deduction requires a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the sponsor that it has exclusive legal control; $250+ gifts need a contemporaneous written acknowledgment. Neither requires periodic account statements.

title: 15 U.S.C. §7001(c) (E-SIGN consumer consent)
summary: Where a law requires information to be provided to a consumer in writing, electronic delivery satisfies it only with affirmative consumer consent after disclosures (paper option, withdrawal, hardware/software).

title: Fidelity Charitable Program Guidelines (CGF-PC-04/24; (c) 2026)
pinpoint: p.4 'Primary Account Holder'; p.15 'Successor Account Holder' (90 days)
summary: Statements, confirmations and communications go to the Primary Account Holder (no frequency stated). If no nominated successor responds within 90 days of notification, the account terminates and the balance becomes unrestricted funds of Fidelity Charitable.

title: Learn how the complaint process works
jurisdiction: US federal (applies to CFPB-supervised companies, not to 501(c)(3) DAF sponsors)
